source.title: Why Post-Norm Transformers Collapse: Attention Amplification and Gradient Repair Failure
source.authors: Xing-Jian Wang; Qingyu Han; Xiaodong Luo; Yin Zhang

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no apparent cutoff or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Reports training-collapse results for 48-layer Post-Norm decoder-only Transformers on C4, a language-modeling setting outside the listed benchmark and architecture versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports initialization-time similarity changes and training-time collapse diagnostics. These are not rows for the listed versions because they do not measure CIFAR classification error, two-layer ReLU local minima, CNN depth with identity shortcuts, the listed initialization comparisons, learning-rate stability behavior, or batch-normalization speed. The paper also cites related findings from other work; those cited results are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study reports Post-Norm Transformer collapse during C4 language modeling, but none of its results measures a listed claim version. It does not compare training across depths or initialization schemes, test identity shortcuts against plain CNNs, measure learning rates relative to a stability threshold, or compare batch normalization with its absence. A new architecture and dataset alone do not make this T3.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that causal attention amplifies token similarity at initialization, growing pre-RMS residual norms weaken gradients reaching earlier layers during collapse, and collapsed runs remain near the frequency loss. Their gradient-contraction theory is conditional, and they explicitly leave the trigger and timing of the abrupt collapse transition unexplained.
record.recipe_differences: Uses AdamW to train decoder-only Transformers for C4 language modeling and measures token similarity, gradients, and cross-entropy loss; the listed versions concern classification, toy teacher-student minima, CNNs, and other training comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: Post-Norm collapse depends on learning rate in the reported comparison: LR=6 × 10−4 remains stable without collapse for 40000 steps, while LR=8 × 10−4 collapses within a few thousand steps. Post-Norm and Pre-Norm differ in initialization-time similarity growth; no Pre-Norm training-collapse comparison is reported in the main text.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-Norm collapse depends on learning rate in the tested C4 Transformer.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A 48-layer Post-Norm decoder-only Transformer trains without collapse at LR=6 × 10−4 but collapses at several higher tested rates; collapsed warmup runs remain near a frequency-loss reference.

fits_no_version.finding: Gradients reaching early layers shrink during the collapse transition.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In collapsing Post-Norm Transformers, increasing pre-RMS residual norms accompany gradient contraction across successive layers, with early-layer gradient norms falling by orders of magnitude.

fits_no_version.finding: Initialization-time attention amplifies token similarity, and subtracting its prefix-averaging component suppresses that growth.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Under the tested Gaussian initialization, causal attention increases token similarity across Transformer layers; removing its prefix-averaging component removes most of that increase.

record.problems: Main backward transition diagnostics center on one run at LR=8 × 10−4, with a repeated-seed diagnostic in the appendix. The main text states that the cause of the sharp transition at a particular optimizer step remains unexplained. Several numerical findings are presented in figures without extracted numeric values.
record.rows_left_out: No rows were omitted under the claim-version rules. Other reported initialization-time similarity measurements and theoretical results concern quantities not named by the listed versions and are not separate rows here.

untested.parts: Training classification error in large convolutional networks on CIFAR-10/100, including random labels and size or regularization comparisons.
Spurious minima and the effect of extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Training-error degradation across CNN depths, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated plain-tanh and Fixup results.

Effects of activation-matched initialization on learning speed and trainable depth, including orthogonal versus Gaussian weights and orthogonal convolution kernels. Initialization variance sweeps here measure token similarity only.
Recovery or divergence relative to a measured initial stability limit, squared-loss catapult dynamics, and full-batch sharpness approaching the stability threshold.
Batch normalization's effects on training speed and learning-rate tolerance, and normalization-free Fixup comparisons.

record.verdict_notes: The row values broadly match the supplied text. States are changed to cannot_determine because they must describe evidence about a listed version; the native collapse findings remain valid. Initialization-only results were explicitly declared omitted in rows_left_out, so they do not require a missing entry.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 classification error, random or corrupted labels, and the listed size, optimizer, and regularization comparisons.
Two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems, spurious minima, and student width relative to teacher width.
Plain batch-normalized convolutional networks, depth sweeps, identity-shortcut comparisons, and the stated ImageNet/CIFAR-10 results.
The listed activation-matched, orthogonal, Gaussian, and convolutional initialization comparisons and their trainability outcomes.
Squared-loss stability thresholds, loss recovery or divergence relative to those thresholds, and sharpness dynamics.
Batch-normalization comparisons on the stated datasets and Fixup comparisons.

rows.size_stated: about 180M parameters; model dimension d = 512, feed-forward dimension dff = 1536, 4 attention heads
rows.operation_detail: AdamW training on C4; run diagnosed for collapse
rows.measure: training loss and last-layer token similarity during training
rows.value: collapses within a few thousand steps; transition occurs at approximately step 2644
rows.note: Collapse and transition timing are stated in text. Post-transition loss is described as staying near the frequency-loss curve; this is language-model loss, not classification error.
rows.check: Collapse near step 2644 at LR=8 × 10−4 is supported, but language-model collapse does not establish any listed version's effect. The extracted observed state describes collapse itself.
